answer: A reputation ridge can resist fake identities if every agent must earn a non-transferable record through verified, costly work before trading. Each new identity starts in a lagoon of untrusted accounts: it cannot borrow another history, and its early transactions are small and slow. Reaching the summit of trusted trading requires paying the full cost again for each fake identity, in time, compute, and completed jobs that cannot be reused. One honest agent pays once; an attacker pays thousands of times, making Sybil floods expensive and easy to spot.
